posts.author: ShigurizuChan
posts.body:
Hello! I'm not exactly new to RPG Maker, but it's the first time in many years I sit down to learn again. Also, first time posting here. I'm trying to make a new (old) project, and I wanted to implement diagonal movement. I'm using JV Master Script, and I found the following issues:
1. When moving diagonally, the player speed increments, I guess because math, and I'd like to know if there is a way to make that not happen.
2. The player sprite overlaps with some tiles (like shown in the example), and I know it's only a visual thing, but I'd like to fix that too. I don't want to use overlapping events to fix that (setting an event with the object sprite and putting it as "same as player"), because I want to save as much memory as possible, and by doing that the map would we  overflowing with events for that sole purpose.
Any ideas?
Thank you
.

posts.author: Zahawk
posts.body:
1. To fix the speed increase, you could try a different diagonal movement script to see if it solves the problem.
DoubleX's Diagonal Movement Script
Victor Sant's Diagonal Movement
It's also possible that your JV Master Script is an old version, and that the latest version fixes that problem. But I was unable to get to the script through wayback so I don't know the version...
2. Are you using tilesets or parallaxes to make your maps?, if its tilesets then all you need to do is have a non-walkable tile [X], then place the visual tiles above it [✰] (VXAce supports 3 layers: ground, decal1, decal2), tiles set to ✰ appear above the player, the X and ✰ are refering to the Database's Tilesets Page where you can set the Passage for tiles. So all your furniture should be set to ✰, then you can either set a duplicate floor tile to X or a transparant decal tile to X
Just realised that depending on the direction you're moving that this will look weird...
Although... if you had duplicate furniture tiles that were only the top half set to ✰, that would solve the problem?

posts.author: Roninator2
posts.body:
ShigurizuChan said:
When moving diagonally, the player speed increments, I guess because math, and I'd like to know if there is a way to make that not happen.
Click to expand...
I don't understand the problem completely. But I think you mean that the time to travel one sqaure diagonally is the same as one square in a 4dir direction. Yes I can see that.
This mod should work for you. unless you change the movement speed during the game then there will need to be a few more adjustments.
Spoiler:
JV Master 8Dir
Ruby:
#==============================================================================
# 8 Dir Move                                                  JV Master Script
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Make player move in 8 dir, supports diagonal pattern.
#==============================================================================

module JvScripts
  module Dirs8
    
    Switch = 0               # Switch id for toggle 4/8 dir, 0 if always 8 dir
    DiagonalSuffix = "_di"   # Suffix for 8 dir charsets
                             # 8 dir charsets include in the first char
                             # the orthogonal and in the second the diagonal
    Diag_Speed = -0.5        # speed reduction for diagonal
    Player_Move = 4          # speed for player movement. default 4
  end
end

#==============================================================================
# Game CharacterBase
#==============================================================================
class Game_CharacterBase
 
  def move_diagonal(horz, vert)
    @move_succeed = diagonal_passable?(x, y, horz, vert)
    if @move_succeed
      @x = $game_map.round_x_with_direction(@x, horz)
      @y = $game_map.round_y_with_direction(@y, vert)
      @real_x = $game_map.x_with_direction(@x, reverse_dir(horz))
      @real_y = $game_map.y_with_direction(@y, reverse_dir(vert))
      increase_steps
    end
    if diagonal_charset?
      set_direction_diagonal(horz, vert)
    else
      set_direction(horz) if @direction == reverse_dir(horz)
      set_direction(vert) if @direction == reverse_dir(vert)
    end
  end
 
  def set_direction(d)
    if !@direction_fix && d != 0
      @direction = d
      @character_index = 0 if diagonal_charset?
    end
    @stop_count = 0
  end
 
  def set_direction_diagonal(horz, vert)
    if !@direction_fix && horz != 0 && vert != 0
      if horz == 4 && vert == 2
        @direction = 2
      elsif horz == 4 && vert == 8
        @direction = 4
      elsif horz == 6 && vert == 2
        @direction = 6
      elsif horz == 6 && vert == 8
        @direction = 8
      end
      
      @character_index = 1
    end
    @stop_count = 0
  end
 
  def diagonal_charset?
    true if @character_name.include?(JvScripts::Dirs8::DiagonalSuffix)
  end
end

#==============================================================================
# Game Player
#==============================================================================
class Game_Player < Game_Character
  def move_by_input
    return if !movable? || $game_map.interpreter.running?
    if JvScripts::Dirs8::Switch > 0
      if $game_switches[JvScripts::Dirs8::Switch] == true
        @move_speed = JvScripts::Dirs8::Player_Move + JvScripts::Dirs8::Diag_Speed
        case Input.dir8
        when 2, 4, 6, 8
          @move_speed = JvScripts::Dirs8::Player_Move
          move_straight(Input.dir4)
        when 1
          move_diagonal(4, 2)
        when 3
          move_diagonal(6, 2)
        when 7
          move_diagonal(4, 8)
        when 9
          move_diagonal(6, 8)
        end
      else
        move_straight(Input.dir4) if Input.dir4 > 0
      end
    else
      if Input.dir8 > 0
        @move_speed = JvScripts::Dirs8::Player_Move + JvScripts::Dirs8::Diag_Speed
        case Input.dir8
        when 2, 4, 6, 8
          @move_speed = JvScripts::Dirs8::Player_Move
          move_straight(Input.dir4)
        when 1
          move_diagonal(4, 2)
        when 3
          move_diagonal(6, 2)
        when 7
          move_diagonal(4, 8)
        when 9
          move_diagonal(6, 8)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
#==============================================================================

posts.body:
ShigurizuChan said:
I should note that it works fine for individual tiles, but when there is one next to another (just like the chair and table), it doesn't
Click to expand...
There are no circumstances where you'd need to use an event over either a "☆" only or both a "☆" and "X" (for these cases of player movement above/below tiles, that I can think of). Yes you'd need an event to add a makeshift fourth tile layer but thats different.
The only positional downside is that if the player is below one of these tiles you'll appear above it when moving diagonally up to it's side (which would look weird for the table legs, etc), but this result is the same for both methods.
So as shown above earlier in 'Events.png' the table would be "☆" and "X", while the chair would be "☆" only. I'm not sure how the player sprite would interact between the top and bottom halves of the chair portion of that sprite, but if the player appears below the top half of the chair and above the bottom half then you'd just need to make the bottom half a "☆" only as well.
